locator: The whole picture: the house from the far side of Prairie Avenue to the south-east, its lit street front on the right (the porch, the stoop, the arched windows and the cornice), the shaded south flank and the south bay's tower to the left, the low stone wall along the walk in front; the neighbour to the north at the right edge. Street trees stand across the front's middle.

note: The fullest picture of the Edson Keith house found. An Italianate house of two storeys over a raised basement under a low hipped roof and a deep cornice on paired scrolled brackets over a panelled frieze; every window round-headed under a hood mould; at the stoop's head a porch on columns whose flat top is a balcony with a balustrade before the arched window over the door; a high stoop whose flights curve out at their foot; a balustraded terrace across the front over the basement lights; a canted bay rising past the cornice as a tower with its own bracketed cornice and cresting; on the roof a balustraded deck and a tall stack. Its attribution to 1906 is the hosting page's; the 1898 Tribune vignette of 1906 draws the same composition (south bay rising as a tower, the porch with its balcony and the arched window over it, the terrace), which is what this project rests the attribution on.
